substantive_theory.goal: Explain transferable local processes of insurgent establishment, reproduction, persistence, relocation, control, collapse, and recurrence.

general_method.goal: Provide a falsifiable partially observed mechanism-based simulation framework with explicit latent state, actor beliefs, observation operators, provenance, synthetic identification, and competitor tests.

comparative_empirical_adjudication.goal: Test the same general mechanisms across heterogeneous cases using frozen case inputs, observation models, holdouts, and simpler competitors.
minimum_generalization_basis: at least two eligible genuine transfer cases
independent control or presence evidence where the claim concerns control or presence

publication_level_gates.requirement: The source used for final historical claims has a settled reproducibility certificate and every reported run is bound to it.
Each central estimand and observation operator used in the paper passes prospective synthetic recovery and relevant null/placebo tests.
At least two genuine transfer cases supply eligible historical evidence for any claim described as general.
The claimed mechanism adds held-out value beyond simpler statistical and reduced-mechanism competitors for the construct actually claimed.
Claim direction survives predeclared plausible observation-model, assignment, case-input, and reporting alternatives.
Nulls, reversals, failed transfers, and failed mechanism cells are reported rather than repaired away or omitted.
Violence is not used as a substitute for control, civilian harm, capacity, regeneration, dependence, or recurrence.

currently_forbidden_conclusions: Pineland has established a stable general theory of insurgency.
The candidate local-reproduction theory is historically validated.
A mechanism is causal because it works in a synthetic world.
A violence predictor is therefore a predictor of control.
A COIN intervention is effective because it reduces simulated violence.
A legacy case run produced under an earlier core is evidence for the current core.
